run.question: Database connection timeouts are occurring for blue-whale app in namespace app-94

report.summary: blue-whale in app-94 addresses its database at DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local:5432, but the Service postgres in app-94 (selector app=postgres-db) has no endpoints, and no postgres backing pod, Deployment or StatefulSet exists anywhere in the cluster. That is the strongest supported explanation for the reported database connection timeouts: the hostname resolves to a Service with no backend addresses. The blue-whale Deployment is 1/1 ready with a single pod created at 2026-11-21T07:08:20-21Z and 0 restarts; the only six events inside the authorized window are that workload's own rollout events (ScalingReplicaSet 0->1, ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate, Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started), with no failure, eviction, OOM or probe events. Application-level impact is not verified by blue-whale's own telemetry: Prometheus and Jaeger were unreachable for this Run, and its pod returned no log lines, so the timeout error text itself was not observed.

claims.text: In namespace app-94 the Service postgres (clusterIP 10.96.216.40, port 5432 -> targetPort 5432) selects app=postgres-db, and its Endpoints object has no subsets (subsets: null), i.e. no backing addresses.

No pod anywhere in the cluster carries app=postgres-db: the cluster-wide pod list (33 pods) contains only blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-bxhkb in app-94 plus kube-system, local-path-storage and otel-demo pods, and no postgres container image appears.

No postgres workload is defined: of the 25 Deployments in the cluster only blue-whale exists in app-94 (image python:3.9-slim, 1/1 ready), and the only StatefulSet cluster-wide is alertmanager in otel-demo.

The blue-whale Deployment's container env is DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local, DB_PORT=5432, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20, command python /app/app.py, and the Deployment reports replicas 1, readyReplicas 1, availableReplicas 1.

The only blue-whale pod, blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-bxhkb, is Running and ready with restartCount 0, container started 2026-11-21T07:08:21Z, owned by ReplicaSet blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 (created 2026-11-21T07:08:20Z), which is owned by Deployment blue-whale.

The only six events with timestamps inside the authorized window are all in app-94 and are Normal rollout events: Deployment blue-whale ScalingReplicaSet ("Scaled up replica set blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 from 0 to 1"), ReplicaSet blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 SuccessfulCreate, and Pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-bxhkb Scheduled, Pulled, Created and Started at 2026-11-21T07:08:20-07:08:21Z.

The blue-whale Service in app-94 does have a backend: Endpoints blue-whale resolves to pod address 10.244.0.103 (targetRef Pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-bxhkb, port 8080), so the missing endpoints are specific to the postgres Service.

The database connection timeouts reported for blue-whale are caused by the postgres Service in app-94 having no endpoints: DB_HOST resolves to postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local:5432, but its selector app=postgres-db matches no pod in the cluster and no postgres Deployment or StatefulSet exists, so connection attempts to the database have no backend.

The current blue-whale pod was created at 2026-11-21T07:08:20-21Z by a 0->1 scale-up at the very end of the sampled window, so whether an earlier blue-whale instance in this window also timed out against the database is not visible in the sampled evidence.

blue-whale shows no crash-level failure at the Kubernetes layer in the sampled state: its pod is Running and ready with restartCount 0, the Deployment is Available/Progressing with 1/1 ready replicas, and the six window events are rollout events with no Failed, Unhealthy, Evicted or OOMKilling reason returned.

Restore a postgres backend whose pods carry app=postgres-db in namespace app-94 (Deployment or StatefulSet plus required volume), or repoint blue-whale's DB_HOST/DB_PORT to a database that exists, then confirm Endpoints postgres gains non-empty subsets.

Re-attempt the observability checks that failed in this Run (Prometheus metric queries, Prometheus rule listing and Jaeger trace service listing all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) so blue-whale's own error rate, span status and latency can be measured against a pre-incident baseline instead of inferred.

gaps: Prometheus was unavailable for this Run: metrics_range_query, get_label_values and list_prometheus_rules all returned status error/SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no metric series (ERROR status counts, latency histograms, kube-state-metrics series) could be read; blue-whale error and latency signals are unknown, not zero.
Jaeger was unavailable for this Run: traces_list_services returned status error/SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span-level evidence of blue-whale database calls or their errors exists in this Run.

blue-whale application logs could not be read: fetch_pod_logs for blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-bxhkb (windows ending 2026-11-21T07:08:59Z and starting 2026-11-21T07:08:00Z) returned status no_data with 0 lines read and no previous container instance, so the timeout error text behind the alert was not observed and the app can be called neither healthy nor failing on its own logs.

The time at which the postgres backend disappeared is unknown: only six events inside the authorized window were returned (all 2026-11-21T07:08:20-21Z), so a deletion or scale-down of a postgres workload before the window cannot be checked (change_history is not integrated).

NetworkPolicies are unknown: the cluster-wide networkpolicies query returned status no_data (zero objects matched), which shows only that the query matched nothing; a policy blocking port 5432 is neither confirmed nor excluded. The resourcequotas query likewise returned no_data, so quota-based blocking of a postgres pod is neither confirmed nor excluded.

The pod's app-code volume is a Secret marked [REDACTED_CREDENTIAL] and cannot be read, so whether the application retries, how it builds its DSN, and whether its own timeout handling explains the reported "timeout" wording rather than an immediate connection refusal could not be verified.
Client-side impact (callers or users of blue-whale) was not measured: no ingress configuration, service-level request metrics or error traces for blue-whale were obtainable in this Run.
next_steps: Check whether a postgres Deployment or StatefulSet for app-94 existed before the authorized window (GitOps/change history is not integrated) and restore it with label app=postgres-db so the postgres Service gains endpoints.
After restoring the backend, verify Endpoints/postgres subsets are non-empty and confirm database calls succeed from a pod in app-94.
Restore Prometheus and Jaeger access and re-check blue-whale ERROR spans, request error rate and duration against a pre-incident baseline.
Have an operator capture blue-whale stdout/stderr directly (the pod returns no log lines) to obtain the exact timeout message and its target address.
